items.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: So he got up on the stage and he had fun with us.

ctx.x: Bill Cosby. But years ago Save a Band came to the State instead of going to the auditorium, I believe the classification was 18 pieces, and Bill Cosby came and he had Sarah Vaughan with him with a quartet, saying Bill Cosby was on the show and then Sarah Vaughan came with her quartet. So the local musicians, they had to bring in 16 more musicians, whatever it was, to make up that classification. And that’s the way it was. And so the union went a little too far sometimes. But anyway he was in the

auditorium one time and he understood all that, but usually when we had these extra musicians we just come and pick up our check and leave. He said, “You guys are going to play?” So I always had a mixed band. So he got up on the stage and he had fun with us. He said, “Not on the white guy, the black guy, come up and play solo; no not the black guy the white guy.” He made fun. The people just roared, he made a joke out of the whole thing. Bill Cosby. But he finally showed up, about a half an hour just ahead of our…
Well he loves jazz too, doesn’t he?
